title: SIM swap fraud - liability of banks and telecom companies
p1:
Your phone number can be stolen without your phone being stolen.

And that simple trick can give criminals access to your bank accounts, OTPs, and digital identity.
p2:
Many people think SIM swap fraud is only the victim's mistake. The surprising part? Liability can depend on whether banks or telecom companies failed to follow proper security checks.

A SIM swap happens when a fraudster convinces a telecom provider to issue a new SIM card linked to your number. Your original SIM stops working, and your calls and messages may be redirected to the attacker.
p3:
Banks are expected to protect customer accounts through reasonable security measures, while telecom companies must verify SIM replacement requests carefully. If a company ignores warning signs or fails basic checks, it may face responsibility depending on the facts and applicable rules.

The practical lesson: treat sudden loss of mobile service as a security emergency, not just a network problem.
conclusion: Do you think banks and telecom companies should share greater responsibility when a SIM swap fraud causes financial loss?
